actions.reasoning: Email claims to be from Chase but the sender address shown is security-alert@chase-notifications-net (missing a normal chase.com domain). The message urges immediate action with a single button link — common phishing pattern. There is no visible account detail (partial account number) or personalized element beyond location; link target is unknown. These are red flags: suspicious sender domain, urgency, single-button CTA, and possible typosquat domain. Because this is LOW trust, do NOT submit any high-risk PII (SSN, full card number + CVV, bank routing/account numbers, or passwords) via links in this email. Instead use official Chase channels (official chase.com site or Chase phone number) to verify the alert.

The email shows multiple phishing indicators (suspicious sender domain, urgent CTA, unknown link target). Under the hard-stop rules for LOW trust, I will not click the 'Secure My Account' CTA or submit any PII. Next safe steps: verify the alert through Chase's official website (type chase.com manually) or call the number on the back of your card; consider reporting the email to Gmail as phishing and changing your Chase password from the bank's site if you suspect compromise.
